original_question: Let g-tilde(n) be the minimum number of products of complete bipartite graphs required so that every element of E(K_n) x E(K_n) lies in an odd number of the chosen products. Determine the values of g-tilde(n).
target_in_paper: Section 13, Question 13.2 (“Covering the product of complete graphs”). The draft is aiming at the paper’s exact open problem asking for the values of \widetilde g(n), not the neighboring asymptotic Question 13.1 about g(n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct parameter, the correct ambient object E(K_n) × E(K_n), the odd-parity covering condition, and the fact that the paper asks for exact values rather than only asymptotics. It is very close to the official formulation of Question 13.2. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
missing_details: The allowed covering pieces should be defined explicitly: in Section 13 they are products of edge sets of complete bipartite graphs, i.e. sets of the form E(K_{a,b}) × E(K_{c,d}), not an unspecified notion of graph product. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

To make the question stand-alone, one should say that these complete bipartite graphs are taken as subgraphs of K_n, so each product is a subset of E(K_n) × E(K_n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

It helps to spell out that the objects being covered are pairs (equivalently, ordered pairs in the Cartesian product) of edges of K_n, since E(K_n) × E(K_n) is the ambient set. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))

The quantifier over n should be explicit (“for each positive integer n”), since the paper states the problem as a function \widetilde g(n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let \widetilde g(n) be the minimum integer m for which there exist complete bipartite subgraphs B_1,C_1,\dots,B_m,C_m of K_n such that every pair (e,f) \in E(K_n) × E(K_n) lies in an odd number of the sets E(B_i) × E(C_i). Determine the exact values of \widetilde g(n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
justification: Section 13 first defines g(n) using partitions of E(K_n) × E(K_n) into products E(K_{a,b}) × E(K_{c,d}), then immediately introduces the odd-cover analogue by allowing each element of E(K_n) × E(K_n) to lie in an odd number of such products and defining \widetilde g(n). The official open problem is exactly “What are the values of \widetilde g(n)?” So the draft should be sharpened only by making the admissible blocks and the ambient set explicit, without broadening to the asymptotic question for g(n) or to the related hypergraph odd-cover parameters \widetilde f_r(n). ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/926651777/A-Collection-of-Open-Problems-in-Celebration-of-Imre-Leader-s-60th-Birthday))
